0.7.5 is a drop-in patch for 0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.7.2, 0.7.3 and 0.7.4: format epoch 3 is unchanged, with no storage, snapshot, WAL or Raft protocol change. Upgrade in place with an ordinary rolling restart (`helm upgrade`). No fresh install or data move is needed.

- **Check `raft.snapshot_build_max_concurrency` before the upgrade** ([#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561)). A configuration that sets it to `0` or to more than `16` no longer loads, so set it to a value between 1 and 16 or remove it. The 0.7.5 chart's schema refuses such a `raft.snapshotBuildMaxConcurrency`, so `helm upgrade` fails before any pod restarts. From 0.7.0, a values file that pins `global.image.tag` or `gateway.image.tag` must move it together with the chart, as for 0.7.1, and from 0.7.3 or earlier the 0.7.4 upgrade notes apply too.
- **The Pi Durable adapter moved to `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula/pi`.** `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula` has no runtime dependencies now, so an application that only attaches files for `node:sqlite` no longer installs Pi Durable and the model SDKs it pulls in. Pi users install `@earendil-works/pi-durable` themselves, in the range `>=1.0.0 <1.2.0` (npm refuses a version outside it with `ERESOLVE`), and import `openUrsulaPiStorage` and `UrsulaPiStorageOptions` from `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula/pi`. Every other export stays in `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula`.
- **Pi errors keep their classes but change their `name`.** Through `openUrsulaPiStorage`, a fenced commit or read rejects with `UrsulaFencedError` and an unknown outcome with `UrsulaReattachError`, both subclasses of `UrsulaReplicationError` with the same `fenced` values and message prefixes. Their `name` is their own, which shows in `String(error)`, the stack and loggers, so match them with `instanceof UrsulaReplicationError`, never by `name`. A statement on a poisoned file that fails with an error that is not an I/O error, such as a constraint violation, now rejects with that error.
- **Attach refuses a file open in the process outside the extension** (`in_use`), on Linux with `/proc` mounted and on macOS, such as a connection opened before the extension was loaded, read-only or not. Close such connections before the attach. An attach that cannot reach the endpoint before its claim throws `UrsulaWriteRefusedError` where it threw SQLite's error, a refused attach has `kind` `refused` where it had `null`, and `attach` and `openUrsulaPiStorage` refuse a stream URL with a query or a fragment (`invalid_url`) before sending anything.
- **The SQLite VFS sends `User-Agent: sqlite-ursula-vfs/0.7.5`** on every request, where it sent ureq's default, `ureq/3.4.2`. Update any proxy, WAF or log rule keyed on the User-Agent before upgrading owners. 0.7.5 changes no format of the extension, so owners upgrade one at a time.
- **The snapshot driver and an operator's snapshot see a build that has just ended** ([#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561)). A group whose trigger went unclaimed is held out of the driver's passes for 0.5 s, doubling for each such trigger in a row up to 16 s, where it sat out 2 to 32 passes. `raft_snapshot_pressure_passes` no longer counts a pass that only carries the same held groups as the pass before it, and the pass log gains `busy`. `POST /__ursula/raft/{group}/snapshot` no longer starts a second build, or waits 5 s and answers `503`, when a build of the group that has just ended covers the request, and a request can now take up to about 30 s, where it took up to about 20 s.
- **`open(streamUrl)` opens a replicated database in one call**, a `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` on a local file named after the stream, and a failure of the extension in it throws an `UrsulaError` whose `action` is `retry`, `reattach`, `stop` or `fix`. SQLite's own errors, such as a constraint violation, stay unchanged. The new classes are `UrsulaError`, `UrsulaFencedError`, `UrsulaReattachError` and `UrsulaSetupError`, and `UrsulaReplicationError`, `UrsulaWriteRefusedError` and `UrsulaPaymentRequiredError` are now subclasses of `UrsulaError`. The docs no longer ask for `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, since attach leaves the file in WAL mode.
- **The SQLite VFS classifies its failures and fences reads.** Every error of its SQL functions starts with `<function>: <kind>: `, and `status(file).error` reports `kind`, `action` and `message` while writes fail. A fenced owner's new read transactions fail (`errcode` 266). After a failed attach the file opens in the process only once an attach succeeds, and a failed attach that wrote nothing into a new file removes the sidecar it created. Writes to an attached file outside the extension are still not detected.
- **The event-time indexer sets `TCP_NODELAY`** on the connections it accepts, as the server and the gateway already did, so a reply that follows another on the same connection no longer waits for the client's delayed acknowledgement.
- **Rust library APIs changed** in `ursula-raft` (`SnapshotBuildCoordinator`, `SnapshotStartError` and the new `SnapshotPermitError`), `ursula-config` (`ValidationError::SnapshotBuildConcurrency` and `RaftConfig::MAX_SNAPSHOT_BUILD_CONCURRENCY`) and `ursula-observability` (`serve::serve_until_shutdown`), with no wire or on-disk change.

Known issues: [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#452](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/452), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#484](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/484), [#490](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/490), [#492](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/492), [#494](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/494), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#497](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/497), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#539](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/539), [#550](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/550), [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561) and [#566](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/566). Every change is listed in the [0.7.5 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#075).
